This document guides AI agents on go-mapi. Read [README.md](README.md) for architecture and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for setup.

**Stack/build/test:** C++ (MinGW), Go, TypeScript/React. `npm run build` (or `npm run build:interceptor|native-host|extension`); tests: `npm run test`.
Flow: Windows App → C++ DLL → JSON files → Go Native Host → Browser Extension → Gmail API.
- `src/interceptor/`: C++; zero dependencies, non-blocking.
- `src/native-host/`: Go; filesystem watching, native messaging.
- `src/extension/`: TypeScript/React; Chrome Identity API for OAuth.

Privacy-focused: keep data local; minimize cloud exposure. Local-first/offline; external calls only when necessary (Gmail sending). Prefer no-cost solutions; ship pragmatically. Use TypeScript strict mode. Keep related code together, minimize files/bloat, colocate related code. Use component-first libraries (React Bootstrap, Radix UI, or similar). No Tailwind; use semantic, maintainable markup. Prepare for translation from the start; use message catalogs/i18n for user-facing strings. Technical documentation remains English.

**Interceptor:** Capture Simple MAPI calls (not Extended MAPI/COM) and write JSON to `%TEMP%\go-mapi\`. Zero external dependencies (no nlohmann/json - hand-rolled JSON). Return immediately; thread-safe for concurrent apps. Files: `main.cpp` (DLL entry/exports), `mapi_impl.cpp` (MAPISendMail), `json_writer.cpp`, `fs_utils.cpp`. Always test with debug build: `npm run build:interceptor:debug`. Test multiple callers (Explorer, PDF viewers, etc.); check memory leaks and thread safety.

**Native host:** Bridge filesystem to extension via Chrome Native Messaging; length-prefixed JSON:
`{"type":"email","id":"...","data":{...}}`, `{"type":"removed","id":"..."}`, `{"type":"ready","version":"1.0.0"}`, `{"type":"process","id":"..."}`, `{"type":"delete","id":"..."}`.
Files: `main.go` (entry/message loop), `protocol.go`, `watcher.go` (fsnotify). Run `gofmt` before committing. Test native messaging with extension; handle deleted files and permission errors.

**Extension:** React 18, React Bootstrap, Vite, TypeScript. Files: `manifest.json` (MV3), `src/background/service-worker.ts` (native messaging/Gmail API), `src/popup/App.tsx`, `src/types/messages.ts`. Use React Bootstrap; keep service worker minimal and offload to popup when possible. TypeScript strict mode is required. Test Chrome and Edge.

JSON files `%TEMP%\go-mapi\*.json` include subject, body, `bodyFormat` (`plain|html`), `to` (name/address), attachments (filename/path/size), and `originApp`; schema: `docs/json-schema.json`.

Docs: README.md user guide; CONTRIBUTING.md developer guide; AGENTS.md technical context; ROADMAP.md phases, not timelines. Comment why, not what; document non-obvious constraints; keep comments concise. Use Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `test:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`.

Workflow:
1. Understand affected component; read relevant sources/patterns; check and run tests; identify related files.
2. Follow patterns; keep changes focused; add tests for new functionality; update docs when behavior changes.
3. Run `npm run build` and `npm run test`; manually test user-facing changes; write clear commit messages.

Personas: C++ Specialist (`src/interceptor/`): minimal, non-blocking, avoid dependencies. Go Developer (`src/native-host/`): filesystem watching/protocol. Frontend Developer (`src/extension/`): React UI/Gmail. DevOps/CI (`.github/workflows/`): Windows builds for all components.

Add JSON field: update `docs/json-schema.json`, C++ `json_writer.cpp`, TypeScript `src/extension/src/types/`, Go structs in `src/native-host/`.
Add setting: Chrome storage API, settings UI, read in service worker, persist with `chrome.storage.sync`.
Manual test: `npm run build`; `npm run register:mapi` (admin); load extension in Chrome/Edge developer mode; inspect `%TEMP%\go-mapi\` JSON and extension DevTools errors.

Decisions: MinGW/GCC over MSVC (simpler, no Visual Studio, Scoop-compatible); React Bootstrap (component-first, semantic; avoid utility-first CSS); JSON files in `%TEMP%` for DLL/native-host communication (simple, debuggable, cross-process, avoids Windows API complexity).
